title: Seeded randomness, the fixed tick and a probe per mechanic, in Rust
note: ctx.rng, ctx.tick and game.probe in Rust: what makes a Rust build measurable and the same on every destination.
intent: The same seed must give the same game in the browser, on the Mac, Windows, Linux and the phones. Every random number comes from ctx.rng (or the rng on_reset receives), time comes only from ctx.dt and ctx.tick, and input only from ctx.keys, ctx.touches, ctx.pointer and ctx.pads inside on_update: the studio steps the game by hand and injects its input there, so anything read from a clock, std's random sources or winit is invisible to every judge (and the lane refuses Instant, SystemTime, thread_rng, HashMap and std's f32 transcendentals; use genex::math and genex::Map). A seed rebuilds the world from World::default() and every facet's state from its own default. Register one probe per mechanic that exists (a count, a phase, a position), a player that returns the real pose, and a demo that drives a mechanic a generic walk cannot reach to an end state a probe can verify.
port: A facet owns src/facets/<slug>.rs and adds exactly its two lines inside the FACET WIRING block of src/main.rs; only the facet that owns the entry edits src/main.rs, src/game.rs or genex.toml, and docs/GENEX_API.md is read-only.

evidence.note: Randomness only from ctx.rng; time from ctx.tick and ctx.dt; genex::math and genex::Map; a facet keeps its own state through game.facet_state::<T>().
